title: Jude and the Autopsy
premise: Retired detective Mara Quintana has traded homicide for a failing seaside bookshop, but when twin letters arrive — one confessing to a drowning thirty years old, the other promising a second death within the month — she is dragged back into a case the police closed long ago. The drowned man was her old partner's brother, and the confession is written in her partner's handwriting, though he has been dead for a decade. As the promised second victim turns up dead in the tidal flats, Mara must unravel alibis woven across thirty years, discovering that a circle of childhood friends built their lives on a shared lie and that her own found family — the shop's odd employees and a runaway teen named Jude — is entangled in it. The killer is the one person who kept faith with the drowned man, and Mara ends the case by choosing truth over loyalty, exposing the confession's author and finally giving the tide back what it took.
about_author: Sebastian Coldharbour is the pen name of a former coastal coroner's assistant who spent twelve years cataloguing what the sea returns. They write mysteries from a houseboat, insisting every fictional body should be treated with the dignity the real ones were denied.

chapters.title: Twin Envelopes
chapters.summary: Mara Quintana, closing her failing bookshop on a storm-lashed pier, receives two letters postmarked the same day: a full confession to a 1994 drowning, and a second note promising 'the next one before the equinox.' Her young employee Jude, a runaway she's informally adopted, witnesses her hands shake for the first time. The beat is dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Mara compares the confession to letters from her late partner, Elias Vane — the handwriting is his, down to the idiosyncratic crossed sevens, though Elias died ten years ago. She visits the retired coroner, Hester Bloom, who confirms the paper is old. The emotional beat: grief reopening like a wound she'd cauterized.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter to 1994: the drowning of Elias's brother Tomás, ruled accidental after a night of drinking at the Saltglass Hotel. Mara, then a rookie, remembers doubting the verdict and being quietly warned off by her own sergeant. The beat is the first crack in her faith in the institution she served.

chapters.title: The Saltglass Circle
chapters.summary: In the present, Mara identifies five surviving members of Tomás's friend group, the Saltglass Circle, all still living within twenty miles: a magistrate, a marina owner, a hospice nurse, a defrocked priest, and a woman who never left town. Each alibi is airtight — too airtight, rehearsed across decades. Beat: cold professional excitement.

chapters.title: Jude's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Jude, shelving true-crime stock, recognizes the Saltglass Hotel from a photograph Jude's late mother kept — she worked there as a cleaner in the nineties. Jude hides this from Mara, terrified of being sent away if connected to the case. Beat: loyalty beginning its war with truth inside the found family.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Alibi
chapters.summary: Mara interviews Magistrate Corliss under the pretext of donating true crime to the courthouse library. His alibi for the night Tomás drowned is corroborated by three witnesses — all fellow Circle members. She realizes the alibis aren't independent; they were constructed together. Beat: the case reframes from one death to a conspiracy of silence.

chapters.title: Equinox
chapters.summary: The promised date arrives. Police find marina owner Declan Foye dead in the tidal flats, staged as a boating accident — but Mara spots the same staging signature from 1994: a watch set to the wrong hour. The detective who once solved three 'accidents' now watches the pattern complete itself. Beat: horror and vindication entwined.

chapters.title: A Watch Told Backwards
chapters.summary: Mara persuades a sympathetic young detective, Imani Reyes, to let her look at Foye's file unofficially. The watch detail was suppressed in 1994 too — meaning someone inside the original investigation protected the killer. Mara suspects her old sergeant, now dead. Beat: the ground of her entire career shifting.

chapters.title: The Nurse Who Prays for Strangers
chapters.summary: Hospice nurse Bridget Halloran, the Circle's softest member, tells Mara that Tomás was alive when the others left the hotel that night — she went back for her gloves. Her guilt has been confessed in prayer for thirty years, but never to police. Beat: the first fissure in the Circle's unity.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Jude, unable to stay silent, secretly visits the defrocked priest, Father Anselm, claiming to research the hotel's history. Anselm recognizes Jude's surname — Jude's mother cleaned the hotel and saw something that night. He warns Jude, gently, that some inheritances are better buried. Beat: Jude now carries a piece of the truth alone.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Siege
chapters.summary: Someone ransacks the bookshop overnight, searching for something and leaving the confession letter's envelope behind — postmarked from the hospice. Mara realizes the killer thinks the letters implicate them and that Jude may have been inside during the search. Beat: the found family's sanctuary is breached; protectiveness hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: Mother's Box
chapters.summary: Jude finally opens the box of their mother's things: a pay stub from the Saltglass, a key to the hotel's linen room, and a page torn from a guest ledger dated the night of the drowning — with one name scratched out. Jude confesses everything to Mara. Beat: the relief and terror of truth-telling; the family bond deepens through honesty.

chapters.title: The Scratched Name
chapters.summary: Mara and Jude reconstruct the ledger name from indentations: it belongs to Elias Vane. Her dead partner was at the hotel that night — and his 'confession' may be genuine, mailed posthumously by someone who found it. Beat: betrayal and grief; the case turns inward, toward the person Mara trusted most.

chapters.title: What Elias Knew
chapters.summary: Mara searches Elias's stored effects and finds a second, unsent confession draft: Elias arrived late that night, saw Tomás struggling in the water, and froze — then helped cover it to protect someone he loved. The draft names no one, but the handwriting analysis confirms the mailed letter is his. Beat: Mara must decide whether to expose her partner's cowardice.

chapters.title: The Priest's Confession
chapters.summary: Anselm, dying of cancer, summons Mara: Elias confessed to him years ago, and Anselm mailed the letters after finding the draft among Elias's papers — but the 'second death' promise isn't Elias's. Someone edited the letter. The killer is using Elias's confession as a weapon. Beat: the mystery pivots from who wrote it to who weaponized it.

chapters.title: Rehearsed for Thirty Years
chapters.summary: Mara maps the alibis against Bridget's timeline and finds the only person whose alibi was never corroborated by an outsider: the woman who never left town, Vera Saltglass, the hotel's owner and Tomás's secret lover. But Vera has advanced dementia — and someone has been speaking for her for years. Beat: sympathy complicating suspicion.

chapters.title: The Voice of Vera
chapters.summary: Jude, visiting Vera to ask about their mother, hears her lucidly murmur that her son — her secret son with Tomás — 'came back to finish the letters.' Vera's caretaker and legal voice is Corliss's clerk, Daniel Murch, who grew up believing Tomás abandoned him. Beat: motive surfaces — a lifetime of inherited lies.

chapters.title: Foye's Last Booking
chapters.summary: Mara and Reyes confirm Murch was at the marina the night Foye died, and that Foye had recently hired a genealogist — he'd discovered Murch's parentage and was going to tell him. The 'promise' letter was Murch's own, mailed alongside Elias's to draw the Circle's sins into the open. Beat: the trap closes; the killer's logic becomes legible.

chapters.title: Before the Tide Turns
chapters.summary: Murch, realizing the net is closing, lures Mara to the Saltglass ruin at low tide with a note in Jude's handwriting — Jude has been taken. Mara goes alone, refusing police backup, torn between procedure and the found family she refuses to lose again. Beat: the loyalty-versus-truth theme made flesh; she chooses the person over the case.

chapters.title: The Saltglass
chapters.summary: In the flooded hotel cellar as the tide rises, Murch forces Mara to hear the full story: Tomás refused to acknowledge him, the Circle covered the accidental drowning to protect their reputations, and Elias froze. Murch wants Mara — the detective who doubted — to declare it murder before the water comes. Jude, bound but unharmed, talks him down by naming his grief honestly. Beat: climax; truth offered as mercy instead of verdict.

chapters.title: What the Sea Returns
chapters.summary: Murch surrenders; Reyes arrests him as the tide gives up Tomás's old watch from the silt, its hands finally matching the true hour of death. The inquest reopens; the Circle's alibis collapse; Corliss resigns. Mara testifies to everything, including Elias's role — choosing truth over her partner's memory. Beat: costly, cleansing resolution.

chapters.title: Open for Business
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the bookshop reopens with a new shelf: local history, honestly told, including Tomás's story. Jude formally stays — papers signed, a room of their own. Mara mails one last letter, to Vera's care home, telling her son's truth gently. The tide goes out clean. Beat: quiet hope; the found family holds.
